CLIMATE NOTE

NOTE
Longwave ridging over the central Plains will strengthen and expand into the Great Lakes through Saturday in response to a closed low near the Four corners opening up across the Rockies with and interaction with additional upper level disturbances/troughing that builds in across the Pacific Northwest. This will reinforce high pressure across the Great Lakes resulting in persistence forecast to end the week. Highs will again push into the upper 60s today, possibly peaking around 70 under mostly sunny skies. Clear skies and light winds overnight will likely lead to patchy or areas of fog, possibly dense, given the supplementation of shallow low-level moisture under the light northeast flow. Fog likely expands from the Thumb and Tri- Cities before pushing into the interior of SE MI before lifting by daybreak. Temperatures then return back into the mid 60s for a high under sunny skies. Outside of radiational fog concerns in the mornings, above normal temperatures under mostly clear skies persists into the weekend. The upper level ridge will flatten Monday into Tuesday over the Great Lakes with a cold front pushing over the state. Limited moisture under a weaker temperature gradient will not bring any concrete rain chances thus PoP values will remain sub 15%, however, flattening of the upper-level will direct better moisture and cloud coverage downstream. Temperatures moderate back towards seasonal normals through at least the early week period. ML-models are much more progressive with the forecasted Pacific trough by the middle of next week relative to the deterministic counterparts, which would again bring about above normal temperatures by the middle of next week if they verify, as the warmer air across the Plains streams into the Great Lakes. && .MARINE... High pressure builds into the Great Lakes today behind a departing weak surface trough. Northeast wind becomes established this afternoon, peaking around 10 to 15 kt. Light flow veers around to southeast on Friday, then becomes more southerly on Saturday as the center of high pressure sinks southward from Quebec toward New England. A slight uptick in wind speeds will be possible this weekend in advance of the next weak trough set to arrive from the northwest. && .PREV DISCUSSION... Issued at 1145 PM EDT Wed Oct 21 2026 AVIATION... Extended stretch of dry and stable conditions will continue under general high pressure. This will limit cloud production outside of some passing cirrus tonight and a lower coverage of diurnal VFR cu Thursday. There remains some potential for shallow fog formation late tonight, with greater probability still focused in the vicinity of MBS/FNT around daybreak. D21/DTW Convection... Thunderstorms are not forecast through the TAF period. DTW THRESHOLD PROBABILITIES... * None. && .DTX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES... MI...None. Lake Huron...None. Lake St Clair...None. .DISCUSSION...

Longwave ridging over the central Plains will strengthen and expand 
into the Great Lakes through Saturday in response to a closed low 
near the Four corners opening up across the Rockies with and 
interaction with additional upper level disturbances/troughing that 
builds in across the Pacific Northwest. This will reinforce high 
pressure across the Great Lakes resulting in persistence forecast to 
end the week. Highs will again push into the upper 60s today, 
possibly peaking around 70 under mostly sunny skies. Clear skies and 
light winds overnight will likely lead to patchy or areas of fog,
possibly dense, given the supplementation of shallow low-level 
moisture under the light northeast flow. Fog likely expands from the
Thumb and Tri- Cities before pushing into the interior of SE MI 
before lifting by daybreak. Temperatures then return back into the 
mid 60s for a high under sunny skies. Outside of radiational fog 
concerns in the mornings, above normal temperatures under mostly 
clear skies persists into the weekend. 

The upper level ridge will flatten Monday into Tuesday over the 
Great Lakes with a cold front pushing over the state. Limited 
moisture under a weaker temperature gradient will not bring any 
concrete rain chances thus PoP values will remain sub 15%, however, 
flattening of the upper-level will direct better moisture and cloud 
coverage downstream. Temperatures moderate back towards seasonal 
normals through at least the early week period. ML-models are much 
more progressive with the forecasted Pacific trough by the middle of
next week relative to the deterministic counterparts, which would 
again bring about above normal temperatures by the middle of next 
week if they verify, as the warmer air across the Plains streams 
into the Great Lakes.

&&

.MARINE...

High pressure builds into the Great Lakes today behind a departing 
weak surface trough. Northeast wind becomes established this 
afternoon, peaking around 10 to 15 kt. Light flow veers around to 
southeast on Friday, then becomes more southerly on Saturday as the 
center of high pressure sinks southward from Quebec toward New 
England. A slight uptick in wind speeds will be possible this 
weekend in advance of the next weak trough set to arrive from the 
northwest.
